correctness.rationale: The two eigenlines contain no nonzero lattice vector: a rational eigenline would give a rational integral eigenvalue dividing the determinant, contrary to hyperbolicity. The reciprocal absolute eigenvalues make L((M^T)^j k)=L(k)+2jχ, and primitive reduction preserves L. At width ≥2χ the closed window hits every progression, including any endpoint residue at equality, so invariance and the circle marginal Fourier tests kill all nonzero coefficients. At smaller width, a lattice direction lies strictly inside the complement of the closed residue arc by density. For even p, the two geometric sums bound each leading-coordinate factor between (β−2)/(β−1) and β/(β−1); the log-ratio error is at most log(β/(β−2)), and pχ(J₊+J₋) is zero modulo 2χ. The expansion differences with digits of magnitude ≤2 have a strictly dominant expanding-coordinate term for β>3, giving dissociation. Each coefficient of the finite probability products stabilizes; density of trigonometric polynomials and compactness give the claimed weak limit. Shifting indices gives M^p invariance, and cyclic averaging preserves the excluded residues. Under the limit product the cosine means are q and the mixed products for distinct indices have expectation q²; under Haar the means and mixed products vanish. Both variance bounds are summable along powers of two, yielding disjoint full-measure sets. Automorphic pushforwards preserve Haar null sets, so the finite cyclic average is singular. The bounded cat-map replay corroborates but does not replace the proof.
residual_risks: The numerical cat-map check is not a uniform or exact-arithmetic proof of the analytic estimates; the proof uses the strict circular gap and the exact digit bounds.
No result for open windows at equality, Euclidean marginals, higher dimensions, or ergodic counterexamples is needed or established.
